thread:
anya: heads up — a customer reported a short outage where traffic fell back to the "degraded" model for ~90s yesterday. console shows a fallback, but not why. can we surface the decision chain?

max: ugh. saw that alert too. logs show a burst of 503s from one region then fallback triggered. question: are we currently sampling telemetry used for trigger evals? iirc we only persist ~10% of request traces.

olivia: correct — sampling at 10% for traces to save ingest costs. metrics (5m buckets) had spikes but not enough signal. fallback logic uses combination of error_rate + concurrent_queue depth + latency SLO. the sampled traces are what feed the decision inspector.

raj: from a product / UX POV we need three things: 1) a compact, human-readable reason string in the console and API response; 2) an audit id so SREs can fetch the full decision trace; 3) a playback mode to re-run the decision engine against preserved metrics for that timeframe.

max: +1. proposing API header: `X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason: error_rate>0.05 && consecutive_failures>=3` and `X-Redwood-Audit-ID: audit_2026_...` so SDKs can log it.

olivia: caution: storing full traces for every fallback will blow up retention costs. different options: a) increase sampling rate only for requests that hit a fallback decision (on-the-fly), b) store compact decision traces (no inputs, just hashes + metric snapshots), c) store full traces for N days behind a toggle.

sre-oncall: (from oncall) b) seems safest — we need reproducible context (metric windows, route chosen, model variant fallback) but not raw user payloads. For incident debug we often need exact prefix lengths + cache state — maybe we can include hashed kv-cache signature instead of prompt text.

anya: agree on privacy constraints. we must avoid logging PII. include prompt_hash and model_kv_signature. also add reason codes that map to human text: e.g. FALLBACK_ERR_RATE, FALLBACK_QUEUE, FALLBACK_KV_MISS.

max: here's a draft compact decision trace format (stored as JSON blob but we won't show full blob in console):

```
{
  "audit_id": "audit_1819001234_42",
  "timestamp": 1819001234,
  "checks": [
    {"name": "error_rate", "window_s": 60, "value": 0.078, "threshold": 0.05, "result": "fail"},
    {"name": "queue_depth", "value": 12, "threshold": 20, "result": "pass"},
    {"name": "latency_p95", "value": 480, "threshold": 500, "result": "pass"}
  ],
  "decision": "fallback_to_degraded",
  "variant": "degraded-v2",
  "prompt_hash": "sha256:...",
  "kv_sig": "kv:abcd1234"
}
```

raj: in the console UI we should show a timeline with the decision node expanded: the short reason + link "view audit" which opens the trace (redacted). also add a small simulator button "replay decision" that runs the decision engine against preserved metric windows. first pass behind feature flag.

olivia: implementation notes: 1) add trigger-level sampling override to the ingress layer so we can snapshot traces for requests that later hit a fallback; 2) store decision blobs in a cold store (30d) and index by audit_id; 3) expose a read-only playback API that returns the decision path (no inputs).

max: also need a UX for rollouts: when a canary triggers automatic fallback, we should show which rollout policy (name + commit) caused the automatic behavior. otherwise folks will blame the model.

anya: can someone file a short RFC? include: storage cost estimate, API header spec, redaction rules, console mockups, and rollout-policy linkage. Target for PR: 2 weeks. I'll take the console mockups. max — can you draft the API headers + decision blob schema? olivia — can you sketch the ingress sampling change and cost calc?

deploy-bot: deployed canary v2 -> prod at 2026-03-18T14:02:00Z :rocket:

sre-oncall: added to incident playbook: if fallback happens, search audit_id within 5m window, run ``replay_decision(audit_id)`` to get root cause.

anya: thanks, team. small followup: limit the console "view audit" to org admins + SRE/Eng to avoid overexposure. privacy + access control first.

max: noted. I'll post the draft API schema later today. :thumbsup:
